I have about two dozen pistols. The third firearm I ever purchased was a Kimber 1911 Stainless, and it was my concealed carry for a long time. It was retired for a XD-S when I took a job that changed my wardrobe to much tigher clothes. The XD-S was eventually retired for a Nighthawk T4.

Kimber makes fine pistols, but there are a few drawbacks. Needing to find a random paperclip to field strip the gun is a rather large drawback (and in my opinion a big "wtf?" in the design), but even bigger are the high number of external safeties which exponentially increases the odds of the weapon not operating when needed.

In the end, buy whatever feels comfortable in your hand and shoots true. With that said, you can make friends with just about any dealer and get any firearm "at cost" or +$30 or so.
